Section 1 of 15

Is It Possible to Look Spiritual and Still Be Far From God?

A person can know religious words, attend services, follow traditions, and appear spiritual while remaining distant from the Creator.

Someone can post Bible verses online and treat people cruelly in private.

A leader can pray in public while using fear and shame to control others.

A person can follow rules mainly to protect a reputation.

It is possible to perform religion without knowing the Creator.

Jesus did not come to create another empty performance. He came to restore a real relationship between God and humanity.

The question is not simply, “Do I look religious?”

The deeper question is, “Does the Creator have my heart?”

What Does Empty Religion Look Like?

Read Isaiah 29:13 ↗.

God described people who honored Him with their words while their hearts remained far away.

They knew what to say. They had learned religious behavior. Yet their relationship with the Creator had become a human routine.

Jesus applied this warning to some religious leaders of His own time.

Read Mark 7:5–9 ↗.

These leaders paid close attention to human traditions while setting aside God’s commands.

A tradition is not automatically wrong. Traditions can preserve memories, teach values, connect generations, and strengthen communities.

The problem begins when a human tradition is treated as if it has more authority than the Creator’s Word.

Every tradition, including the traditions of churches and religious institutions, must be examined by Scripture.

Religion Can Become a Mask

Read Matthew 23:25–28 ↗.

Jesus described people who appeared clean on the outside while hiding corruption within.

A spiritual appearance can become a mask used to hide:

  • Pride
  • Greed
  • Secret habits
  • Dishonesty
  • Sexual wrongdoing
  • Uncontrolled anger
  • Abuse of power
  • Lack of compassion
  • Desire for attention
  • Fear of what others will think

The Creator sees beyond the mask.

This may feel uncomfortable, but it is also good news. You do not have to pretend with God. He already knows what is inside, and He still invites you to come closer.

Healing begins when hiding ends.

Jesus Confronted Religious Hypocrisy

Jesus was gentle with people who knew they were struggling. He was much more direct with leaders who used religion to control others while refusing to examine themselves.

Read Matthew 23:1–12 ↗.

Some leaders wanted titles, attention, and positions of honor. They placed heavy burdens on other people but did little to help carry those burdens.

Jesus taught that true leadership looks like service.

Read Matthew 23:23–28 ↗.

These leaders focused on small outward details while neglecting justice, mercy, and faithfulness.

Jesus did not say that careful obedience was unimportant. He said that outward obedience without justice, mercy, and faithfulness revealed a serious problem in the heart.

Religious authority never gives anyone permission to mistreat people.

A spiritual leader should become more humble, honest, accountable, compassionate, and willing to serve.

The Creator Does Not Ask You to Pretend

Some people learn to hide questions because they fear being judged.

They may wonder:

What if I do not understand everything?

What if I still struggle with doubt?

What if my life is not as put together as it appears?

What if religion has hurt me?

What if I am afraid of trusting another spiritual leader?

The Creator is not threatened by honest questions.

Read Psalm 62:8 ↗.

God invites you to pour out your heart before Him.

The Bible contains prayers from people who felt afraid, confused, angry, abandoned, or full of doubt. They spoke honestly with the Creator instead of performing for Him.

Read Psalm 13:1–6 ↗.

David asked God how long he would feel forgotten. He did not hide his pain behind religious words.

A real relationship has room for honesty.

How Did Jesus Describe True Worship?

Read John 4:4–24 ↗.

Jesus met a Samaritan woman beside a well. Jews and Samaritans had a long history of religious and cultural conflict. They disagreed about the proper place to worship.

Jesus did not avoid her because she belonged to another people. He spoke with her, listened, revealed truth, and offered her living water.

When she asked about worship, Jesus explained that true worship would not be controlled by one mountain or another location.

The Creator seeks people who worship Him in spirit and truth.

Worship in spirit comes from a heart made alive by the Holy Spirit.

Worship in truth agrees with what the Creator has revealed in Scripture and through Jesus.

Sincerity alone is not enough. A person can sincerely believe something untrue.

Correct information alone is also not enough. A person can know biblical facts while having a proud and unloving heart.

The Creator wants both spirit and truth.

Does the Creator Live Only in Certain Buildings?

Read Acts 17:24–28 ↗.

The Creator does not live only in temples or buildings made by human hands. He made the world and gives life to everyone.

A building can provide a helpful place to gather, learn, pray, and encourage one another. But entering a religious building does not automatically bring a person close to God.

The Creator can hear you:

  • At home
  • Outdoors
  • In your car
  • At work
  • In a hospital
  • In a dorm room
  • In a crowded city
  • In a quiet rural community
  • In a place where no one else knows you are praying

No institution owns access to Him.

Through Jesus, you can approach the Creator directly.

Read Hebrews 4:14–16 ↗.

You do not need to wait for a human leader to give you permission to pray.

What Does the Creator Want Most?

A religious leader once asked Jesus which commandment was most important.

Read Mark 12:28–34 ↗.

Jesus answered that we should love the Creator with all our heart, soul, mind, and strength. He added that we should love our neighbors as ourselves.

Love is the center of a real relationship with God.

This love is more than an emotion. It includes loyalty, trust, time, attention, and obedience.

Read Deuteronomy 10:12–13 ↗.

The Creator asks you to walk in His ways, love Him, serve Him, and follow His commands.

He wants your whole heart because He wants your whole life to become free and complete.

Obedience Can Come From Different Motives

Two people may perform the same action for very different reasons.

One person obeys because of fear:

“If I make one mistake, God will stop loving me.”

Another obeys to gain attention:

“I want people to see how spiritual I am.”

Another obeys to feel superior:

“I follow the rules better than those people.”

Another obeys from love:

“The Creator rescued me. I trust His way, and I want my life to honor Him.”

The outward action may look similar, but the Creator sees the motive.

Read 1 Samuel 16:7 ↗.

Human beings look at outward appearances. God looks at the heart.

Healthy obedience grows from love and trust.

Read 1 John 5:2–3 ↗.

God’s commands are not a price we pay for salvation. They describe how people live when love is changing their hearts.

What Is Wrong With Trying to Earn God’s Approval?

Trying to earn acceptance places the focus on your performance.

You begin measuring yourself:

Did I pray long enough?

Did I read enough?

Did I make fewer mistakes than someone else?

Does God like me more today?

This creates pride when you think you are succeeding and despair when you fail.

Read Luke 18:9–14 ↗.

Jesus described two men who went to pray.

One listed his good behavior and compared himself with other people. The other admitted his need for mercy.

Jesus said the humble man went home right with God.

The Creator is not impressed by spiritual competition.

Your acceptance rests on what Jesus has done, not on your ability to outperform someone else.

What Is Real Faith?

Read Hebrews 11:6 ↗.

Faith means believing that the Creator exists and trusting that He responds to those who seek Him.

Real faith affects choices.

Read James 2:14–18 ↗.

If someone claims to have faith but refuses to help a person in need, the claim is empty. Actions do not purchase salvation, but they reveal whether faith is alive.

An apple tree does not produce apples to become an apple tree. It produces apples because it is alive and rooted.

In the same way, compassion, obedience, honesty, and service grow from a living relationship with the Creator.

What Kind of Religion Does the Bible Accept?

The Bible does not say that every form of religion is bad.

Read James 1:26–27 ↗.

James describes pure religion as controlling our speech, caring for vulnerable people, and refusing to be corrupted by the world.

Read Isaiah 58:3–10 ↗.

The people in this passage practiced fasting, but they continued exploiting workers, arguing, and ignoring people in need.

God rejected their performance.

The Creator said true devotion should lead them to loosen oppression, share food, provide shelter, and care for others.

Prayer and fasting matter. Their true purpose is to bring us closer to the Creator so that His character becomes visible in our lives.

A spiritual practice that never produces mercy, justice, humility, or changed behavior has missed its purpose.

How Can You Recognize Spiritual Manipulation?

Religious language can be used to guide people toward the Creator. It can also be used to control them.

Be cautious when a leader or group:

  • Treats honest questions as rebellion
  • Demands loyalty that belongs to the Creator
  • Uses fear to control personal decisions
  • Pressures people to give money they cannot afford
  • Claims that leaders cannot be questioned
  • Protects reputation instead of protecting people
  • Uses shame to keep harmful behavior secret
  • Separates people from safe family and friends
  • Treats one race or culture as spiritually superior
  • Makes promises the Bible does not make
  • Focuses more on power than service

Read 1 Peter 5:2–3 ↗.

Spiritual leaders are called to care for people willingly and lead by example rather than control.

Read Acts 17:11 ↗.

You have the right to compare every teaching with Scripture.

Respect does not require silent agreement. Trustworthy leadership welcomes careful questions and honest accountability.

How Should Cultural Practices Be Examined?

Culture shapes language, family life, food, music, art, celebrations, relationships, and the way people understand the world.

The Creator does not ask people to become culturally empty.

At the same time, no culture is the final authority for truth. Every culture contains practices that reflect beauty and practices that may need correction.

This is true of Native cultures, European cultures, popular culture, religious culture, and every other human culture.

Ask clear questions about any practice:

  • What does this practice mean?
  • Who or what does it honor?
  • Does it agree with Scripture?
  • Does it direct worship to the Creator alone?
  • What kind of character does it produce?
  • Does it protect human dignity?
  • Does it involve spiritual powers or guidance outside the Creator?
  • Can I participate while remaining fully loyal to Jesus?

Do not condemn an entire culture because of one belief or practice. Examine each question carefully, honestly, and with respect.

The same standard should be applied to practices introduced by churches or dominant society.

What Does a Real Relationship With the Creator Produce?

Read John 15:1–12 ↗.

Jesus said that people who remain connected to Him will produce fruit.

A growing relationship with the Creator produces:

  • Greater honesty
  • Humility
  • Desire for Scripture
  • Willingness to obey
  • Compassion for people
  • Strength to resist sin
  • Courage to admit wrong
  • Patience with others
  • Concern for justice
  • Freedom from spiritual pride
  • Desire to serve
  • Love that becomes action

Growth may be slow. You may still have struggles. The question is whether your life is moving closer to Jesus.

A real relationship changes the direction of your life before every part of your character has reached maturity.

What If You Do Not Feel Close to God?

Feelings change.

You may feel close to the Creator during a meaningful prayer and distant from Him the next morning. Stress, exhaustion, grief, depression, conflict, or disappointment can affect your emotions.

The Creator’s presence does not depend on whether you feel it.

Read Hebrews 13:5–6 ↗.

God promises not to leave or abandon you.

Read Psalm 42:5–11 ↗.

The writer spoke to his own discouraged heart and chose to continue hoping in God.

When you do not feel close to the Creator:

  • Speak honestly with Him.
  • Continue reading Scripture.
  • Remember what He has already done.
  • Examine whether you are knowingly holding onto sin.
  • Ask the Holy Spirit to guide you.
  • Spend time with trustworthy people who strengthen faith.
  • Care for your physical and emotional health.
  • Continue obeying the truth you understand.

Faith sometimes means remaining with the Creator when strong feelings are absent.

How Can You Build a Real Relationship With Him?

Speak honestly

Prayer is a real conversation with the Creator. Tell Him what you are grateful for, what hurts, where you are confused, and where you need help.

Listen through Scripture

Read slowly. Ask what the passage reveals about God, people, and the choice before you.

Respond to what you learn

Knowledge without response becomes another form of empty religion.

Read James 1:22–25 ↗.

Practice the truth the Creator shows you.

Make room for quiet

Constant noise can keep you from examining your heart. Create short periods without a screen, music, or conversation.

Confess quickly

When the Holy Spirit reveals sin, bring it to God instead of hiding.

Serve someone

Love grows stronger when it becomes action.

Stay connected

A personal relationship with the Creator does not require spiritual isolation. Find trustworthy people who respect Scripture, welcome questions, and reveal the character of Jesus.

What Does the Creator Want From You Today?

Read Micah 6:6–8 ↗.

The prophet asked whether God wanted larger and larger religious offerings.

The answer was clear.

The Creator calls us to:

  • Act justly
  • Love mercy
  • Walk humbly with Him

He does not need an impressive performance.

He wants your honest heart.

You can begin with a simple prayer:

“Creator, remove anything false in me. Teach me to know You, love You, and walk with You in truth.”

Think About It

Write your answers in your own words.

  1. What is the difference between appearing spiritual and knowing the Creator?
  2. Have you ever felt pressure to hide an honest spiritual question?
  3. What human tradition have you assumed was a command from God?
  4. Which motive most often influences your obedience: fear, attention, comparison, or love?
  5. What does worshiping in spirit and truth mean to you?
  6. Which signs of spiritual manipulation are most important to recognize?
  7. What cultural or religious practice would you like to examine more carefully through Scripture?
  8. What fruit is your present spiritual life producing?
  9. What is one way your relationship with the Creator could become more honest?
  10. What act of mercy or service can you practice this week?

Try This During the Coming Week

Set aside fifteen quiet minutes each day.

Read one passage:

  • Day 1: Isaiah 29:13–16 ↗
  • Day 2: John 4:4–26 ↗
  • Day 3: Matthew 6:1–18 ↗
  • Day 4: Luke 18:9–14 ↗
  • Day 5: Isaiah 58:3–12 ↗
  • Day 6: James 1:19–27 ↗
  • Day 7: John 15:1–12 ↗

After reading, write down:

  • What does this passage reveal about empty religion?
  • What does it reveal about a real relationship with the Creator?
  • What motive do I need to examine?
  • What truth can I put into practice today?

Choose one act of devotion that no one else needs to see. Pray privately, help someone quietly, forgive a debt, encourage a hurting person, or give without seeking recognition.

Let it be an honest gift of love to the Creator.

A Prayer You Can Pray

Creator God, I do not want to hide behind spiritual words or outward behavior. I want to know You as You truly are. Examine my heart and show me where pride, fear, selfishness, or the desire for approval has shaped my faith. Help me worship You in spirit and truth. Give me courage to ask honest questions and wisdom to test every teaching by Your Word. Protect me from manipulation and keep me from using Your name to control others. Grow justice, mercy, humility, obedience, and love within me. Help my life reveal the character of Jesus. Amen.

Remember This

It is possible to appear spiritual while remaining far from the Creator.

Human traditions must be tested by Scripture.

The Creator welcomes honest questions and sincere prayer.

True worship includes both the Holy Spirit and biblical truth.

Religious activity cannot earn God’s acceptance.

Real faith produces obedience, compassion, justice, and service.

No spiritual leader stands above Scripture or honest accountability.

Every culture and religious tradition must be examined by the same standard.

A real relationship with the Creator changes the direction and fruit of your life.

The Creator wants your honest heart rather than an impressive performance.
